The segment features a bearded man in a black hoodie and baseball cap, who is speaking directly to the camera. He is wearing glasses and uses expressive hand gestures, particularly when emphasizing key points. To the left of him, there is a visual aid with Arabic text and its English translation. The Arabic text is "وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَن ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَىٰ," and the English translation, according to Sahih International, reads, "And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind." The man interprets this text to explain the consequences of not turning towards or remembering Allah, describing it as leading to a "depressed life". Later in the segment, the scene shifts to a split-screen displaying blurred images of two people in separate video calls; one person wearing a yellow shirt on the left, and another in a black shirt on the right. The background of the initial scene is a mix of blue and green tones, with a leather couch and books visible in the background.

The video segment is about Sana, who broke up with her partner Melvin. The video begins with a medium shot of a man with a beard and glasses, wearing a black hoodie and a black baseball cap. He is sitting in front of a microphone and speaking to the camera. He gestures with his hands and looks directly at the camera. The background consists of books, a plant, a speaker, and a YouTube plaque. Next, a photo is shown of a man wearing a black quilted jacket. The video then returns to the bearded man sitting in the same position, speaking to the camera. Next, the video switches to an out-of-focus split screen showing a man on the left and a woman on the right. Text appears below that reads, "I wasn't losing sleep because I lost some gem of a man, but to think how silly I was. How silly! And how I wasted myself, by joining my name with a donkey" (Ich habe keinen Schlaf verloren, weil ich ein Juwel von einem Mann verloren habe, aber zu denken, wie dumm ich war. Wie dumm! Und wie ich mich verschwendet habe, indem ich meinen Namen mit einem Esel verbunden habe). The video then returns to the bearded man, who says "*ALLEGEDLY." He then says that infidelity and physical abuse occurred. Next, a blurred video shows a woman who states that she has photos of him hitting her and that she broke her head and has bruises on her face. Next, the bearded man explains that she was mentally affected and started taking sleeping pills. The video then shows blurred footage of a woman in a red dress. A woman is shown in a split-screen talking. She says, "Unfortunately, I was on sleeping tablets. I will not recommend that to anybody. And I think the day I stopped it was the day my mom got to know about it. Then, I started you know reciting more and more and more, and that's how I started getting more sleep. And I was like, 'Didn't I tell you that, I never thought in my life I would be praying to sleep from Allah.'" (Leider war ich auf Schlaftabletten. Ich würde das niemandem empfehlen. Und ich glaube, der Tag, an dem ich damit aufgehört habe, war der Tag, an dem meine Mutter davon erfahren hat. Dann habe ich angefangen, immer mehr zu rezitieren, und so habe ich angefangen, mehr Schlaf zu bekommen. Und ich sagte mir: "Habe ich dir nicht gesagt, dass ich nie in meinem Leben gedacht hätte, dass ich von Allah um Schlaf beten würde?""

Alright, here’s a description of the video segment. The video begins with a man, wearing a black cap and glasses, speaking directly into a microphone. He is bearded and dressed in black. To his left, the screen shows an Instagram post by ‘sanakhaan21’, including the text ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Brothers and sisters! Today I am talking to you standing at a crucial juncture of my life; there I have been living the Shobiz (Film Industry) life for years, and during this time I have been blessed with all kinds of fame, honour and wealth from my fans for which I am grateful to them. But for a few days now, I have been possessed of the realization that: Is the real purpose of man’s coming into this world only to chase wealth and fame? Isn’t it a part of his/her duty to spend his/her life in the service of those who are needy and helpless? Shouldn’t a person think that he/she could die at any moment? And what will happen to him after he/she is no more? I have been searching for answers to these two questions for a long period of time, especially the second question as to what will happen to me after my death? When I searched for the answer to this question in my religion, I realized that this life in the world is actually for the betterment of life-after death. And it will be better if the slave lives according to the command of his Creator, and does not make wealth and fame his only goal; rather, he/she should avoid sinful life and serve humanity, and follow the path shown by his/her Creator. Therefore, I declare today that from today onwards, I have resolved to say goodbye to my Shobda Lifestyle forever and serve humanity and follow the orders of my Creator. All brothers and sisters are requested to pray for me to Allah to accept my repentance and grant me the true ability to live in accordance with my determination of spending my life following the commandments of my Creator and in the service of humanity, and grant me perseverance in it. Finally, all brothers and sisters are requested to not consult with regards to any Shobiz work henceforth. Thank you very much Sana Khan’ (Sana Khan expresses gratitude and speaks about changing her lifestyle to align with religious principles and service to humanity). Below the post, it says ‘Liked by muftimenkoficial and 303,711 others’. The man references the content of the post, using gestures and facial expressions to emphasize his points.
